messages:
emma: Hey docs team — small QA: the trace hook snippet in the Console Observability quickstart shows `trace.set_attribute('cost_usd', cost)` after the span ends. That causes our SDK to not pick up the attribute in the dashboard sample. Anyone seen this?
ryan: Yup, saw it — the attribute needs to be set before span.end() because we attach attributes to the active span. I made a tiny PR but it's blocked on a link fix. @matt (SRE) can you approve the change? :eyes:
matt (SRE): on it, can you paste the snippet?
emma: Here's the snippet I'm seeing:
```python
with tracer.start_span('generate') as span:
    # do work
    span.set_attribute('tokens_generated', 123)
    span.set_attribute('cost_usd', 0.003)
# incorrect: attributes after span closed
# span.set_attribute('latency_ms', 12)
```
ryan: also note older SDKs named set_attribute -> set_attr, we should add a compatibility note and link to the SDK migration guide: https://redwood.dev/sdk-migration
emma: thanks — I'll add the note and update the dashboard example to show where the cost/latency breakdown picks up attributes. I'll open a docs PR and tag everyone.
infra-bot: Deploy preview created: https://deploy.preview/PR-4321 :white_check_mark:
matt (SRE): quick approval, but can we rename `cost_usd` -> `telemetry.cost.usd` per naming conventions? See style guide: https://redwood.dev/docs/telemetry-naming
ryan: fine with that. Emma, can we also add a tiny test snippet that asserts attributes exist before span end? Keeps regressions away.
emma: yes — adding unit test and a one-liner in the PR description. ETA EOD today. Thanks :tada:
